subject: SLO discovery: latency & throughput budgeting — next steps and pilot proposal
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acmetech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLO discovery: latency & throughput budgeting — initial recap

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap so we have aligned next steps and inputs for a pilot: 

Summary of what you shared:
- Targeted user-facing reliability: p95 latency target ~250ms for responses around ~350–512 tokens (chat completions).
- Sustained throughput expected: ~200 reqs/min; short-term burst up to ~300 reqs/min for 5–10 minutes.
- Concurrency estimate: ~100 concurrent active requests under steady state.
- Streaming: ~40% of interactions need partial/streaming responses (chat UX).
- Typical prompt + response size: ~450 tokens total.

Initial cost/perf levers we discussed (high-level):
- Continuous batching: reduces per-token overhead at the cost of small added batching latency; good for sustained QPS.
- Prefix/KV caching: effective if a high % of requests share common prompts or system messages (saves compute on early tokens).
- Quantization profiles: redwood-medium-8q gives a good compute/cost balance; redwood-large-16q improves quality but increases tail latency and cost.
- Model variants + fallback: canary smaller variant for most traffic with automatic fallback to larger model for quality-sensitive requests.

Deliverables from Redwood (next actions we committed to):
1) Run micro-benchmarks with your sample payloads (if you can share) to produce a SLO-fit matrix (p50/p95/p99 across model variants + quant profiles).
2) Produce a cost projection (CSV attached: redwood_cost_model_v2.csv) and a latency budget spreadsheet (attached: latency_budgets.xlsx) showing expected unit costs for continuous batching vs low-latency config.
3) Proposal for a 2-week pilot (canary + telemetry) we can start in the week of Dec 7 — includes tracing, token-level cost breakdown, and automated fallback rules.

Questions for you to confirm (quick):
- Can you confirm whether the 250ms p95 is an end-to-end client-side requirement or server-side (origin) latency target?
- Do you have sample payloads (typical prompts + expected completions) we can use for the bench?
- Is 40% streaming a firm number or a ballpark? If it varies, any peak streaming percent?

If you’re good with that plan I’ll schedule the bench run and loop in engineering for the pilot plan.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: latency_budgets.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_cost_model_v2.csv (CSV)
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acmetech.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:01:12 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO discovery: latency & throughput budgeting — initial recap

Diego —

Thanks for the clear recap, this matches our notes. A few clarifications before you run benchmarks: 

1) The 250ms p95 is measured end-to-end in our product (client to final token), but we care most about the server-side contribution. For the pilot, if you can report server-side p95 and an estimated network egress + client render number, that will help.
2) Peak burst is more like 300–350 reqs/min for ~10 minutes during a morning refresh. Sustained outside bursts is around 180–200/min.
3) Streaming ratio is currently around 40% average but can spike to ~60% in short windows.
4) p99: we prefer to keep p99 under 800ms if possible — will that be feasible with the smaller quantized variants?

I’ll attach a sanitized sample payload set (truncated) to a follow-up email — trying to get EngOps to sign off on sharing. We also prefer the Dec 7 pilot week.

Can you confirm whether your latency_budgets.xlsx includes server-side only and that the cost model assumes continuous batching enabled?

Appreciate it,
Alex
Head of Product, AcmeTech
alex.jones@acmetech.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 18:05:30 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO discovery: latency & throughput budgeting — internal follow-up

Quick internal note: 
- I agree with the proposed bench and pilot. We should baseline on redwood-medium-8q (best cost/latency tradeoff) and include redwood-large-16q as an option for quality validations.
- Add an automated canary route: 10% traffic to large model for a week, measure quality improvements, then adjust.
- I'll pick up the micro-benchmark runs once Alex shares sample payloads — Ben, can you prepare a short mutual action plan draft (deliverables, owners, timeline) we can propose to them?

I'll also include a suggested fallback policy to disable continuous batching for requests that hit <100ms budget for client responsiveness.

Laura
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acmetech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO discovery: latency & throughput budgeting — initial recap

Alex — thanks for the fast turnaround. Answers inline and next steps below.

> The 250ms p95 is measured end-to-end in our product (client to final token), but we care most about the server-side contribution.

Good question — for the benchmark we will report: server-side p50/p95/p99 (service-to-token), plus an estimated network egress + render budget. In the spreadsheet attached the latency_budgets.xlsx tab named "server_budget" is server-only numbers.

> Peak burst is more like 300–350 reqs/min for ~10 minutes

Noted — we'll parameterize the bench to run both sustained (200rpm) and burst (350rpm) phases so you can see the SLO tail behavior under each.

> Streaming ratio can spike to ~60%

We'll run streaming-enabled benches at 40% and 60% to show differences in token emission latency and cost. Streaming adds a small per-request overhead but reduces perceived latency for users.

> p99 target under 800ms

We expect medium-8q with continuous batching to hit p95=250ms server-side in your distribution; p99 will likely be between 400–700ms depending on prompt length and burst behavior. We'll show tradeoffs for Q4_0 vs Q8_0 quant profiles in the SLO-fit matrix.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- By Mon Nov 23: Alex shares sanitized sample payloads + any synthetic peak profiles (or permission to replay production traces).
- Nov 24–30: Redwood runs micro-benchmarks (sustained + burst + streaming ratios) and produces SLO-fit matrix + cost CSV.
- Week of Dec 7: 2-week pilot (canary + telemetry + fallback policies).
- Before pilot: Ben to send a short mutual action plan and telemetry checklist; Laura to share suggested canary/fallback config.

If that all works, I’ll open a HubSpot deal record (linked) and schedule the kickoff call.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-202611

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
